# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Gatault_2015_eculizumab"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Gatault_2015_eculizumab"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1080/19420862.2015.1086049> (open access, PMC4966484)

Gatault et al. measured free serum eculizumab troughs in nine adults on
maintenance therapy and fitted a one-compartment model with parallel linear
and Michaelis-Menten elimination in Monolix 4.3.2. Clearance depends on body
weight. A separate in vitro regression links free eculizumab to terminal
complement activity (C9 neoantigen ELISA). The authors combined the two to
project steady-state troughs and complement activity against body weight for
1200 mg given every 14, 28 or 42 days (their Figure 4). Both parts are
packaged here: `Cc` is free eculizumab (ug/mL) and `tca` is the predicted
terminal complement activity (arbitrary units).

# Population

Nine adults (median age 40.9 years, range 23.9-67.0; 7 female; all Caucasian)
treated at Tours University Hospital, France: seven with atypical
hemolytic-uremic syndrome (aHUS; two kidney transplant recipients) and two with
paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria (PNH) (Table 1). Weights were 50-92 kg,
median 63 kg (Table 2). Dosing followed the label: aHUS 900 mg weekly for 4
weeks, 1200 mg at week 5, then 1200 mg every 2 weeks; PNH 600 mg weekly for 4
weeks, 900 mg at week 5, then 900 mg every 2 weeks. 97 stored pre-infusion
samples were assayed, with a dense inter-infusion profile in Patient 6 and
post-discontinuation samples in Patient 2.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Gatault_2015_eculizumab")()$population`.

# Source trace

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| `lvc` | log(3.2 L) | Results, 'Eculizumab clearance' (RSE 10%) |
| `lcl` | log(0.18 L/day) at 63 kg | Results, 'Eculizumab clearance' (RSE 7%) |
| `lvmax` | log(5.0 mg/day) | Results (printed '5.0 mg/L/day', RSE 4%); unit read as an amount rate, see Assumptions |
| `lkm` | log(1.1 ug/mL) | Results (printed '1.1 mg/L', RSE 33%) |
| `e_wt_cl` | 2.5 | Results: 'beta_WT = 2.5, p<0.0001'; covariate model in Methods, 'Pharmacokinetic study' |
| Reference weight | 63 kg | Median of the Table 2 weights; Results call 63 kg 'medium-weight' |
| `etalvc` | 0.150^2 = 0.0225 | Results: IIV SD of V 15.0% |
| `etalcl` | 0.146^2 = 0.021316 | Results: IIV SD of CL 14.6% |
| No IIV on Vm, Km | -- | Results; Supplement 'Results for the base model' (variances set to 0, shrinkage > 90%) |
| `propSd` | 0.25 | Results: proportional SD 0.25 (RSE 1.6%); Supplement: proportional error retained |
| `lrbase_tca` | log(20.6) | Methods: A = 20.6 x exp(-0.084 x C); Figure 5 |
| `lslope_tca` | log(0.084 mL/ug) | Same equation |
| `d/dt(central) = -CL/V * central - Vm * C/(Km + C)` | -- | Methods and Supplement 'Structural model' (one compartment, first-order + Michaelis-Menten elimination) |
| `CL = 0.18 * (WT/63)^2.5` | -- | Methods covariate model; power form confirmed from Figure 4 (below) |
| `tca = 20.6 * exp(-0.084 * Cc)` | -- | Methods, 'Measurement of eculizumab trough levels' |

# Typical-value helpers

```{r helpers}
mod <- readModelDb("Gatault_2015_eculizumab")
mod_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)

# Steady-state trough: dose every `ii` days until `horizon`, observe just
# before the next (omitted) dose. 2520 days is a common multiple of 14, 28 and
# 42 and more than 30 linear half-lives at the lightest weight simulated.
ss_trough <- function(model, wt, dose, ii, horizon = 2520) {
  ev <- data.frame(
    id = 1L, time = c(seq(0, horizon - ii, by = ii), horizon),
    evid = c(rep(1L, horizon / ii), 0L),
    amt = c(rep(dose, horizon / ii), 0), cmt = "central", WT = wt
  )
  s <- rxode2::rxSolve(model, events = ev, rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-10)
  as.data.frame(s)[nrow(s), c("Cc", "tca")]
}
```

# Replicate Figure 2: washout after discontinuation (Patient 2)

Patient 2 (54 kg, aHUS) stopped eculizumab after more than three years of
1200 mg every 14 days. The paper prints the concentrations 54 and 62 days
after the last infusion (90 and 38 ug/mL); the other points were digitised by
the maintainers from Figure 2.

```{r figure-2}
fig2_obs <- data.frame(
  time = c(0, 25, 39, 54, 62, 67, 81, 95),
  Cc = c(467, 255, 137, 90, 38, 0, 0, 0)
)
washout <- function(model) {
  t_last <- 1400
  ev <- rbind(
    data.frame(time = seq(0, t_last, by = 14), evid = 1L, amt = 1200),
    data.frame(time = t_last + seq(0.01, 100, by = 0.5), evid = 0L, amt = 0)
  )
  ev$id <- 1L
  ev$cmt <- "central"
  ev$WT <- 54
  s <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(model, events = ev))
  s$time <- s$time - t_last
  s
}
fig2_sim <- washout(mod_typ)

ggplot(fig2_sim, aes(time, Cc)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(data = fig2_obs, shape = 18, size = 3) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 50, linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(
    x = "Days after last eculizumab infusion", y = "Free eculizumab (ug/mL)",
    title = "Figure 2: Patient 2 after discontinuation",
    caption = "Line: typical 54-kg patient from the packaged model. Points: Figure 2."
  )

at <- function(s, t) approx(s$time, s$Cc, xout = t)$y
fig2_cmp <- fig2_obs |>
  filter(time %in% c(25, 39, 54, 62)) |>
  mutate(sim = at(fig2_sim, time), pct_diff = 100 * (sim / Cc - 1))
knitr::kable(fig2_cmp, digits = 1, caption = "Typical-value washout vs Figure 2.")
# Deterministic typical-value solve against the observed points: about
# +20 / +19 / -18 / +16 %. A Vm, V or CL slip moves these by far more.
stopifnot(all(abs(fig2_cmp$pct_diff) < 30))
```

The typical 54-kg patient follows the observed decline within about 20%,
including the accelerating fall below ~50 ug/mL where the saturable pathway
dominates.

# Steady-state troughs by patient (Table 2, Figure 1)

Each Table 2 patient is simulated at their own weight and maintenance dose
(1200 mg every 14 days for aHUS, 900 mg every 14 days for PNH) with 100
virtual subjects carrying the model's IIV. Doses are given as IV bolus over
50 intervals (700 days, at least 9 linear half-lives at every Table 2
weight), and the last interval (day 686-700) goes to PKNCA. The induction
phase does not affect steady state and is omitted.

```{r cohort}
tab2 <- data.frame(
  patient = 1:9,
  WT = c(63, 54, 50, 92, 59, 56, 81, 65, 87),
  disease = c(rep("aHUS", 7), "PNH", "PNH"),
  dose = c(rep(1200, 7), 900, 900),
  obs_trough = c(468, 468, 733, 55, 376, 366, 107, 187, 161)
) |>
  mutate(treatment = sprintf("Pt %d (%s, %g kg, %g mg)", patient, disease, WT, dose))

n_per <- 100L
make_patient <- function(i) {
  p <- tab2[i, ]
  ids <- (i - 1L) * n_per + seq_len(n_per)
  doses <- expand.grid(id = ids, time = seq(0, 686, by = 14))
  doses$evid <- 1L
  doses$amt <- p$dose
  obs <- expand.grid(id = ids, time = 686:700)
  obs$evid <- 0L
  obs$amt <- 0
  bind_rows(doses, obs) |>
    mutate(cmt = "central", WT = p$WT, treatment = p$treatment)
}
events <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(tab2)), make_patient)) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(events[events$evid == 0, c("id", "time")]))

rxode2::rxSetSeed(20151086)
sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = events, keep = c("treatment", "WT"))
```

```{r figure-1}
typ_trough <- tab2 |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(typ = ss_trough(mod_typ, WT, dose, 14)$Cc) |>
  ungroup()

sim_trough <- as.data.frame(sim) |>
  filter(time == 700) |>
  group_by(treatment, WT) |>
  summarise(
    Q05 = quantile(Cc, 0.05), Q50 = median(Cc), Q95 = quantile(Cc, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  left_join(tab2[, c("treatment", "disease", "obs_trough")], by = "treatment")

ggplot(sim_trough, aes(WT)) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = Q05, ymax = Q95, colour = disease), width = 1.5) +
  geom_point(aes(y = Q50, colour = disease), shape = 1, size = 2.5) +
  geom_point(aes(y = obs_trough, colour = disease), shape = 4, size = 3) +
  labs(
    x = "Body weight (kg)", y = "Steady-state trough (ug/mL)",
    title = "Steady-state troughs vs weight (cf. Figure 1, Table 2)",
    caption = "Circles and bars: simulated median and 5th-95th percentiles. Crosses: Table 2 mean observed troughs."
  )

knitr::kable(
  typ_trough |>
    mutate(ratio = obs_trough / typ) |>
    select(treatment, obs_trough, typ, ratio) |>
    rename("Patient" = treatment, "Observed mean trough (ug/mL)" = obs_trough,
           "Typical-value trough (ug/mL)" = typ, "Observed / typical" = ratio),
  digits = 2, caption = "Table 2 mean troughs against the typical-value steady-state trough at each patient's weight and dose."
)
gm_ratio <- exp(mean(log(typ_trough$obs_trough / typ_trough$typ)))
gm_ratio
# Deterministic: 1.25 with the packaged model. Reading Vm as 5 mg/L/day
# (16 mg/day) gives 1.83, and CL = 0.09 L/day gives 0.45.
stopifnot(gm_ratio > 1.0, gm_ratio < 1.5)
```

The typical-value troughs reproduce the strong inverse weight dependence of
Figure 1. The observed means sit on average 25% above the typical
predictions, consistent with nine patients whose individual estimates were
used in the fit (Figure 3) and with 15% IIV on CL and V. The two largest
under-predictions are Patient 9 (PNH, 87 kg; observed 3.5-fold above the
typical value) and Patient 1 (63 kg; 1.6-fold). At 87 kg and 900 mg the
steep weight exponent puts the typical trough near the range where the
saturable pathway takes over, so small differences in CL move it a lot.

# PKNCA validation

```{r pknca}
sim_nca <- as.data.frame(sim) |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, treatment)
dose_df <- events |>
  filter(evid == 1, time == 686) |>
  select(id, time, amt, treatment)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sim_nca, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | treatment + id, route = "intravascular")
intervals <- data.frame(start = 686, end = 700, cmax = TRUE, cmin = TRUE, auclast = TRUE)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

published <- tab2 |>
  transmute(treatment, cmin = obs_trough)
cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_res,
  reference = published,
  by = "treatment",
  params = "cmin",
  units = c(cmin = "ug/mL"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "Simulated median Cmin over the steady-state interval vs Table 2 mean observed trough. * differs by >20%.")

summary(nca_res)
```

The paper reports only troughs. Seven of the nine patients are within 20%
of the simulated median Cmin. Patients 1 and 9 sit well above it, as in the
typical-value table above. The paper gives no per-patient estimates to
compare against.

# Replicate Figure 4: weight-based projections

Figure 4 shows steady-state troughs and complement activity against body
weight for 1200 mg every 14, 28 and 42 days. The trough values below were
digitised by the maintainers from Figure 4.

```{r figure-4}
fig4_dig <- data.frame(
  ii = c(rep(14, 8), rep(28, 6), rep(42, 5)),
  WT = c(30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80, 90, 100, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 100, 30, 40, 50, 60, 80),
  Cc = c(6100, 2870, 1570, 920, 560, 350, 220, 130, 2750, 1250, 640, 340, 180, 21, 1650, 720, 340, 170, 26)
)
grid <- expand.grid(WT = seq(30, 140, by = 10), ii = c(14, 28, 42))
proj <- function(model, label) {
  out <- grid
  r <- Map(function(w, i) ss_trough(model, w, 1200, i), grid$WT, grid$ii)
  out$Cc <- vapply(r, function(x) x$Cc, numeric(1))
  out$tca <- vapply(r, function(x) x$tca, numeric(1))
  out$model <- label
  out
}
mod_cl009 <- mod_typ |> rxode2::ini(lcl = log(0.09))
fig4_sim <- bind_rows(
  proj(mod_typ, "Packaged model (CL = 0.18 L/day)"),
  proj(mod_cl009, "Diagnostic: CL = 0.09 L/day")
)

ggplot(fig4_sim, aes(WT, Cc, colour = factor(ii))) +
  geom_line(aes(linetype = model)) +
  geom_point(data = fig4_dig, shape = 1, size = 2.5) +
  labs(
    x = "Body weight (kg)", y = "Steady-state trough (ug/mL)", colour = "Interval (days)",
    linetype = NULL, title = "Figure 4: steady-state trough vs body weight, 1200 mg",
    caption = "Circles: digitised Figure 4."
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.box = "vertical")

ggplot(fig4_sim, aes(WT, tca, colour = factor(ii))) +
  geom_line(aes(linetype = model)) +
  labs(
    x = "Body weight (kg)", y = "Complement activity (arbitrary units)", colour = "Interval (days)",
    linetype = NULL, title = "Figure 4: predicted complement activity at the steady-state trough"
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.box = "vertical")

fig4_cmp <- fig4_dig |>
  filter(Cc >= 20) |>
  left_join(fig4_sim, by = c("WT", "ii"), suffix = c("_fig", "_sim")) |>
  mutate(ratio = Cc_sim / Cc_fig) |>
  group_by(model) |>
  summarise(median_ratio = median(ratio), max_abs_log_ratio = max(abs(log(ratio))), .groups = "drop")
knitr::kable(fig4_cmp, digits = 2, caption = "Simulated / digitised Figure 4 troughs (points >= 20 ug/mL).")
stopifnot(
  # Deterministic. The packaged model sits at about a third of the Figure 4
  # troughs (median ratio 0.34) ...
  with(fig4_cmp, median_ratio[model == "Packaged model (CL = 0.18 L/day)"] < 0.7),
  # ... while halving CL alone reproduces the digitised points (median ratio
  # 0.91, max |log ratio| 0.28), which pins the weight exponent and Vm unit.
  with(fig4_cmp, abs(log(median_ratio[model == "Diagnostic: CL = 0.09 L/day"])) < 0.15)
)
```

**Figure 4 is not reproduced by the published estimates.** The packaged model
gives about one third of the Figure 4 troughs (median simulated / digitised
ratio 0.34). Halving CL to 0.09 L/day, with nothing else changed, reproduces
the nineteen digitised points (median ratio 0.91, every point within about
30%). That CL is not used, for three reasons:

* the paper's own half-life, 12.4 days at 63 kg, equals ln(2) x 3.2 / 0.18;
* the observed troughs (Table 2) and the Patient 2 washout (Figure 2) agree
  with CL = 0.18 L/day, while CL = 0.09 L/day over-predicts the Table 2
  troughs about 2-fold and keeps Patient 2 above 350 ug/mL at day 62
  (observed 38);
* the estimates are printed in the text, while Figure 4 is a derived
  projection.

The packaged model therefore puts the weight thresholds for 4- and 6-weekly
dosing at lower weights than the paper's 90 kg and 70 kg. The diagnostic
curve still settles the structural questions: with Vm read as 5 mg/day and CL
as a power of weight with exponent 2.5, the whole family of Figure 4 curves is
matched by a single change of scale in CL.

# Half-life against weight

```{r half-life}
hl <- data.frame(WT = c(40, 63, 100), paper = c(19.5, 12.4, 7.8)) |>
  mutate(model = log(2) * 3.2 / (0.18 * (WT / 63)^2.5))
knitr::kable(hl, digits = 1, caption = "Linear (target-independent) half-life, days.")
```

The paper states that the half-life falls from 19.5 days at 40 kg to 7.8 days
at 100 kg. Those two values scale as weight to the power 1, not 2.5, so they
contradict the reported exponent. The exponent of 2.5 is kept because Figure 4
needs it: the typical CL back-solved from Figure 4 at each weight has a
log-log slope of 2.44-2.56 across the three intervals.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Vm unit.** The Results print Vm = 5.0 'mg/L/day'. The model is encoded
  with Vm as an amount rate, 5.0 mg/day, in `d/dt(central) = ... - Vm * C/(Km + C)`.
  This is the convention of Monolix's PK library, which the authors used, and
  three checks support it. Read as 5.0 mg/L/day x 3.2 L = 16 mg/day, the model
  (i) takes Patient 2 to zero by day 54 after the last dose, where 90 ug/mL
  was observed (Figure 2); (ii) under-predicts the Table 2 troughs 1.8-fold
  (geometric mean) against 1.25-fold for 5 mg/day; and (iii) cannot reproduce
  Figure 4 for any CL, V or exponent (best sum of squared log errors 3.8,
  against 0.014 for the amount reading with CL, V and exponent free).
* **Covariate equation.** Methods print the covariate model as
  'ln(theta_i) = ln(theta) = beta_WT . (WT/med(WT))', which is garbled. It is
  read as the Monolix log-transformed covariate,
  ln(CL_i) = ln(CL) + 2.5 x ln(WT/63), a power model. Fitting Figure 4 with a
  linear-exponential form exp(beta x (WT/63 - 1)) instead gives a sum of
  squared log errors about 90-fold worse.
* **Reference weight.** 'med(WT)' is not printed. 63 kg is the median of the
  nine Table 2 weights, and the Results call 63 kg the medium weight.
* **Weight on V.** Only the CL effect is reported, so V has no weight effect.
* **Figure 4 and the half-life text** disagree with the printed estimates, as
  shown above. The printed estimates are packaged.
* **IIV.** Monolix reports omega as a standard deviation. 15.0% and 14.6% are
  read as omega = 0.150 (V) and 0.146 (CL), so the variances are 0.0225 and
  0.021316. IIV on Vm and Km was set to zero by the authors and is omitted.
* **Complement activity** comes from an in vitro regression on spiked pooled
  sera (7 samples, 20-166 ug/mL) and has no reported residual error. It is
  returned as a derived quantity, `tca`, not as a fitted endpoint. Complete
  blockade (< 0.5 units) corresponds to Cc > 44 ug/mL.
* **Infusion.** The paper does not give an infusion duration. Doses are
  simulated as IV bolus, which has negligible effect on troughs given the
  multi-day half-life.
* **Errata.** No correction notice was found in Europe PMC (searched
  2026-11-24).
